 Prayer:
 Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitut  praying to issue a Writ of Mandamus, to direct the respondents t  an award, under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency   land acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 with   to land in Survey No.30/3A1B measuring an extent of 437 sq.metre  situated at Elayampalayam Village, Thiruchengode Taluk, Namakkal  District fixing land value for sum of Rs.22,91,685.00/- without   amount deduction for development charge.
For Petitioner : Dr.M.Devendran

For Respondent : Mr.P.Sathish, AGP  ORDER This writ petition has been filed to direct the respondents to pass an award, under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in land acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 with regard to subject land.

3. By consent of the parties, the main writ petition is taken up for disposal at the admission stage itself.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that in this case, initially, the respondents had initiated the land acquisition proceedings with regard to the subject land for forming By-Pass road.
In this regard, 2nd respondent had issued a notice dated 02.07.2025 under Section 19(5) of Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001 to the petitioner for submitting objections.

Subsequently, though an objection was filed by the petitioner, later he has agreed to receive the award amount under protest based on the promise made by the respondent that they will not deduct 1/3rd amount from land value for developing charges.
Under these circumstances, now, the respondent orally called for an enquiry and stated that the land value will be fixed only after deducting 1/3 rd amount.
In this regard, the petitioner had filed a representation dated 08.09.2025, requesting the respondents not to deduct any amount from the land value.
However, the said representation was not considered by the respondents till date.
Hence, this petition.

sentences.text: In reply, the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondent would submit that the representation filed by the petitioner will be considered and appropriate orders will be passed within a period of 4 weeks.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondents and also perused the materials available on record.
7.
In the case on hand, the 2nd respondent had issued a notice dated 02.07.2025 under Section 19(5) of Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001 to the petitioner for acquiring the subject land.
According to the petitioner, he has agreed to receive the award amount only based on the promise made by the respondent that they will not deduct 1/3 rd amount from land value for developing charges.
However, it was submitted that now, the respondent has orally called for an enquiry and stated that the land value will be fixed only after deducting 1/3rd amount.

Thereafter, the petitioner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/10/2025 07:14:37 pm ) had filed a representation dated 08.09.2025, requesting the respondents not to deduct any amount from the land value.
However, the said representation was not considered by the respondents till date.

8. In view of the above, this Court directs the respondents to consider and dispose of the petitioner's representation dated 08.09.2025, on merits and in accordance with law, after affording sufficient opportunities to the petitioner, within a period of 4 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
9. With the above directions, this writ petition is disposed of.
No cost.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is also closed.
